name: PixelTransition-TS-TW

frames.best_why: Frame 3 shows the trip details already readable through a scattering of white pixels.

tagline: White pixels scatter to swap a mountain photo for trip details.
summary: A photo card breaks into a grid of white squares on hover, settling into a dark panel of route details; leaving dissolves it back to the photo.
appearance: A white-bordered card showing a blue-green mountain valley, with a small caption below outside the frame. During the change a grid of white squares scatters over the face, uncovering white text on near-black beneath.
behaviour: Hovering or focusing fires white pixels in random order across the card, swaps the photo for the trip panel at the peak, then clears the pixels. Leaving runs the same sequence in reverse.
demo_content: Mountain valley photo; back reads "Trek · 6 days", "Dolomites High Route" and "from $1,240".
search_phrases: trip card reveals details on hover
blocky reveal animation for a picture
use_when: A card needs to hide selling details behind an image until the visitor shows interest.
avoid_when: Its second face is only revealed on hover, focus or tap, so it is easy to miss on a quiet page.
customise: Both faces are content props, alongside grid size, pixel colour, step duration, one-shot mode, aspect ratio, className and style. Nothing inside the faces is editable.
weight_why: Up to 144 plain divs shown and hidden by one GSAP stagger; it only runs on hover.

a11y.note: Focus and tap trigger the reveal and the inactive face is aria-hidden, but there is no visible focus ring and no reduced-motion handling.

issues: Mid-transition frames leave text half hidden behind white blocks, which reads as broken.
The 300px default width overrides the container unless a className is supplied.
polish_why: The dissolve is well paced and both faces are designed; mid-transition noise is the weak point.
title: Pixel Dissolve Transition
